result.title: Robust LLM Data Selection via Content-Invariant Gradient Attribution
result.summary: Gradient-based data attribution has become an important tool for high-quality data selection in the instruction fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs), as it estimates the contribution of training examples through their influence on model optimization. However, we find that existing global gradient attribution methods suffer from surface-form bias: minor changes to semantically irrelevant details, such as wording or formatting, can produce highly inconsistent attribution scores even when the underlying content remains unchanged. To address this issue, we propose Content-Invariant Gradient Attribution (CIGA), a robust framework for instruction data selection. CIGA first identifies layers whose gradients are both influential for attribution and stable under semantics-preserving surface-form perturbations, thereby reducing formatting noise in gradient features. It then dynamically fuses these attribution signals with semantic representations of the input, combining optimization-level influence with content-level information. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks show that CIGA produces more stable rankings under surface-form perturbations while preserving downstream capabilities and improving average performance. CIGA also reduces attribution cost, offering a robust and efficient approach to data selection for LLM instruction tuning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文发现全局梯度数据归因存在表面形式偏差：措辞或格式等语义无关的改动会使归因分数剧烈波动；为此提出 CIGA，先筛出对归因有影响且在语义保持扰动下梯度稳定的层，再与输入的语义表示动态融合，用于 LLM 指令微调数据选择，在多个基准上提升了扰动下的排序稳定性与下游性能并降低成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按语义保持扰动筛选稳定梯度层」的思路可能可供核查 latent 推理轨迹中的贡献分配与格式噪声抑制；但论文面向纯文本指令数据筛选，与视觉状态或推理期 latent 生成无直接联系，需较多核查。
